builds.name: Reference: Ranked mid core
builds.goal: Reference for Yasuo: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ mid players use most (13,879 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 57.5% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: A mobile melee critical fighter who uses enemy units as dash routes, builds a knockup and punishes airborne targets. The current mid provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Immortal Shieldbow → Infinity Edge → Death's Dance. Lethal Tempo keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Berserker's Greaves, Guardian Angel, Bloodthirster.
builds.summary: The proven mid baseline: Immortal Shieldbow → Infinity Edge → Death's Dance, with Lethal Tempo.
testPlan: Play it in mid as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Immortal Shieldbow → Infinity Edge → Death's Dance) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 57.5% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Immortal Shieldbow → Infinity Edge → Death's Dance.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.
builds.author: Rift Build Lab ranked data

kitEvidence.formula:
Yasuo thrusts, dealing [20 / 45 / 70 / 95 / 120 + (1.05) × AD] physical damage. If he hits, he gains a stack for [6] seconds. While he has 2 stacks, his next use of this Ability fires a whirlwind from range, dealing the same damage and Knocking Up for [1] second.

If used while dashing, this Ability strikes in a circle rather than a stab.

Yasuo dashes through a target, dealing [70 / 85 / 100 / 115 / 130 + (0.2) × AD[statFormula=2] + (0.6) × AP] magic damage. Each use of this Ability grants [(70 / 85 / 100 / 115 / 130 + (0.2) × AD[statFormula=2] + (0.6) × AP) × (0.25)] bonus damage to subsequent uses for [5] seconds, stacking up to [4] times.

This Ability has a [10 / 9 / 8 / 7 / 6] second per-target Cooldown.

Yasuo teleports to an Airborne enemy champion, dealing [200 / 350 / 500 + (1.5) × AD[statFormula=2]] physical damage and holding all nearby Airborne enemies up for an additional [1] second. Yasuo also gains maximum Flow, but loses all {{Spell_YasuoQ1Wrapper_Name}} stacks.

Afterwards, Yasuo's critical strikes ignore [60]% bonus Armor for [15] seconds.

Resolve: Moving grants Flow, which is tracked on Yasuo's resource bar. Moving faster grants more Flow. At maximum Flow, damage from a champion or monster briefly grants [characterLevelInterpolation(125 → 600; raw flags preserved)] Shield.

Intent: Yasuo's Critical Strike Chance is increased by [100]% but his Critical Strike Damage is reduced to [(1) × Stat(9)]. Gain @YasuoCritToAD*.01@ Bonus Attack Damage for every 1% Critical Strike Chance above 100%.
Yasuo creates a drifting wall of wind that blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds.

builds.name: Dash AP Flow
builds.summary: Test AP on a finite chain of distinct-target E dashes.
builds.goal: Test AP on a finite chain of distinct-target E dashes.
builds.hypothesis: E deals 0.6 AP magic damage and increases subsequent E damage up to four stacks, subject to per-target cooldowns. Cosmic responds to magic damage, Riftmaker rewards extended combat and Lich Bane requires a real follow-up attack. Movement grants Flow, so faster relocation can alter shield availability.
testPlan: Required state: Several distinct dash targets, E stack duration maintained and finite Flow recorded.
Measure successive E hits on separate targets at zero through four stacks and shield availability after the path.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Isolated opponents deny E chains; sacrificing crit reduces Q and ordinary attack threat.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: The same target cannot be redashed immediately simply because E's cast cooldown is short.
Confidence: speculative. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Cosmic Drive, Riftmaker, Lich Bane, Nashor's Tooth, Rabadon's Deathcap, Sorcerer's Shoes. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Situational adaptation: Physical matchup
builds.goal: Situational adaptation for Yasuo: adapt to the specified fight rather than assume one universal build
builds.hypothesis: A mobile melee critical fighter who uses enemy units as dash routes, builds a knockup and punishes airborne targets. Account for kit crit/attack-speed rules and Q cooldown limits. Dash units and airborne setup are real constraints; excess attack speed need not create faster Q forever. Armor and access may turn survival into additional attack/spell windows.
builds.summary: Armor and access may turn survival into additional attack/spell windows.
testPlan: Kit question for Yasuo: Account for kit crit/attack-speed rules and Q cooldown limits. Dash units and airborne setup are real constraints; excess attack speed need not create faster Q forever.

Start with the early core (Stridebreaker, then matchup armor) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Compare against the reference route at the same level, gold spent, finite stacks and opponent setup. Record unused gold; isolate an item change before changing runes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Resource: Flow. Do not treat mana regeneration as Flow recovery; Nimbus replaces Manaflow when that Sorcery row is used.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: Armor and access may turn survival into additional attack/spell windows. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern. Choose the opponent profile this defensive route is intended to address, then repeat against the wrong damage type.

Q evidence: Thrusts forward, damaging all enemies in a line.

On hit, grants a stack of Gathering Storm for a few seconds. At 2 stacks, Steel Tempest fires a whirlwind that knocks Airborne.

Steel Tempest is treated as a basic attack and scales with all the same things. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: Randuin is conditional on the enemy attack/crit profile; it costs an offensive slot.

The route fails Yasuo's stated kit question: Account for kit crit/attack-speed rules and Q cooldown limits. Dash units and airborne setup are real constraints; excess attack speed need not create faster Q forever.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: Randuin is conditional on the enemy attack/crit profile; it costs an offensive slot.
Full cost 16,100 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
Counter-items are conditional. Change boots/defense for the real matchup, then record the modified setup.
buyOrder: Stridebreaker, then matchup armor. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Randuin's Omen, Spirit Visage, Sterak's Gage are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Resource: Flow. Do not treat mana regeneration as Flow recovery; Nimbus replaces Manaflow when that Sorcery row is used.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.

builds.name: Last Breath three attacks
builds.summary: Use R's post-cast armor interaction for a short critical attack follow-up.
builds.goal: Use R's post-cast armor interaction for a short critical attack follow-up.
builds.hypothesis: R requires an airborne champion and grants maximum Flow; afterward critical strikes ignore bonus armor for fifteen seconds. Fiendhunter offers three enhanced basic attacks after R and movement from Stridebreaker helps contact. Yasuo's passive doubles crit chance, so a finite crit budget reaches its cap quickly.
testPlan: Required state: Valid airborne target, R used and three follow-up attacks within the item window.
Compare three post-R attacks versus pre-R against equal total armor with different bonus-armor shares.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: No knockup denies R or peel stops attacks; low enemy bonus armor reduces the special penetration value.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: R's bonus-armor ignore is not a blanket reduction to all armor for every spell.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.

Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
